# Vow — edition 2026 (v0)

> Vow is a strict, typed language for code written by agents. Every function signature states its parameter types (with refinements), result, effects, and error union; the compiler checks the body against it. Read this whole file; it is the entire core language. Library signatures: `vow doc --search` or the `symbol_query` tool.

## Toolchain loop
`vow check --json` (types/effects, holes allowed) → `vow test --json` → `vow run`. Diagnostics have stable codes (`V3001`), byte spans, and `fixes[]` with an `impact` class; never apply a fix whose impact is `contract_change` or `authority_change` without being asked. `vow fmt` is canonical. `vow explain V3001` gives the rationale. Holes `?name` compile under `check` and report expected type, locals, and candidates.

Status (pre-alpha): `vow check` parses, resolves, and type/effect-checks; `vow run`/`vow test` are not wired yet. `std/fs`, `http`, `sql`, `cli`, `ai`, `decimal` are designed, not written.

## Syntax in one screen
```vow
import std/http.{Request, Response}        // first segment = package; no wildcards
import std/sql as db

type Email = String where String.len(it) <= 254 && String.contains(it, "@")   // refinement, `it` = value
type User = { id: Int, email: Email, name: String }                            // nominal record
type Shape = Circle(Float) | Rect(Float, Float) | Empty                        // variants, positional fields
error NotFound(id: Int)                                                        // error tag with payload
error Forbidden
type UserError = NotFound | Forbidden                                          // error union (tags only)

effect Users {                                                                 // user-defined effect
  fn get(id: Int) -> Option<User> ! {Fail<SqlError>}
}

pub fn view(caller: String, id: Int) -> User ! {Users, Log, Fail<UserError>} // signature = contract
  requires id > 0                                                            // runtime-checked, caller blamed
  ensures result.id == id                                                    // runtime-checked, callee blamed
{
  let found = try { Users.get(id) } catch { SqlError { .. } => None }         // catch removes tags from the row
  match found {                                                              // exhaustive
    None => fail NotFound { id },
    Some(u) if u.name != caller => fail Forbidden,
    Some(u) => u,                                                            // last expression = value
  }
}

pub fn main() -> Unit ! {Console, Sql, Log} {
  with Users.sql(), Log.json() {                                             // install handlers (innermost last)
    let u = view("ann", 7)
    Console.print("hello {u.name}")                                          // interpolation needs Show
  }
}

test "missing user" {
  with Users.memory([]) { expect_fail(fn() { view("ann", 1) }, NotFound { id: 1 }) }
}
property "clamp bounded"(x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) requires lo <= hi { expect(clamp(x, lo, hi) <= hi) }
```

Rules you must know:
- Casing is enforced: `snake_case` values/functions/modules/effect-row variables (`e`); `PascalCase` types, variants, error tags, effects, type variables (`A`).
- Statements end at newline. A line continues only if it ends with an operator/`(`/`[`/`{`/`,`/`=`/`->`/`=>`/`.` or the next line starts with `.`, `else`, `catch`, a closing bracket, or a binary operator other than `-`. `foo\n(bar)` is two statements. `;` is allowed.
- Blocks are expressions; the value is the final expression. `return e` exits the function early. `if` without `else` is `Unit`. An unused non-`Unit` value is an error (`V2040`): write `let _ = e`.
- Top-level `fn` must be fully annotated. Omitted `!` means pure `! {}`. Inside bodies everything is inferred.
- `<...>` is type arguments only in type positions. No call-site type args: `let xs: List<Int> = List.empty()`. In expressions `<` is comparison.
- `e.f(a)` means `T.f(e, a)` where `T` is `e`'s type and `f` lives in `T`'s module (`List.map`, `String.len`, your own module for your types). `Type.f` is a module function or constructor; `Effect.op(...)` performs an operation.
- No `null`, no exceptions, no implicit conversions, no overloading, no methods/classes/traits, no macros, no mutable references, no globals.
- Record literal: `User { id: 1, email, name: "x" }` (punning ok). Update: `User { ..u, name: "y" }`. Not allowed unparenthesized in `if`/`match`/`with`/`for`/`while` headers.
- Tuples `(a, b)`, `.0`/`.1`; lists `[1, 2]`; `xs[i]` is `List.get(xs, i) -> Option<T>`; ranges `0..n` (exclusive).
- Lambdas: `fn(x) { x + 1 }` or `fn(x: Int) -> Int { x + 1 }`. One form.
- `var` locals can be reassigned (`total = total + x`; `u.name = "y"` means `u = User { ..u, name: "y" }`; `xs = List.push(xs, 1)`). Closures capture by value and cannot assign outer vars. `let` is immutable.
- Loops: `for x in xs { }` (List, Range, Map → `(k, v)`, Set), `while c { }`, `break`, `continue`.
- Operators: `+ - * / %` (`Int` with `Int`, `Float` with `Float`; `+` also concatenates `String`), `== != < <= > >=`, `&& || !`. `Int` arithmetic is checked: overflow and `/ 0` are defects (crash the task), not errors. Convert explicitly: `Int.to_float`, `Float.round`.
- Patterns: `_`, `x`, literals, `Some(x)`, `User { id, .. }`, `(a, b)`, `[]`, `[x, ..rest]`, `A | B`, guards `if`. Matches must be exhaustive; `_` is required for `Int`/`String` literals.

## Types
Primitives `Unit Bool Int(i64) Float(f64) String(UTF-8) Bytes Never`. Data `List<T> Map<K,V> Set<T> Option<T>(None|Some) Result<T,E>(Ok|Err) Range (A,B)`. Everything is immutable and compared structurally. Built-in constraints (derived automatically, not user-definable): `Eq Ord Hash Show Schema` — `fn sort<A: Ord>(xs: List<A>)`. Functions, handlers, resources, and `Secret<T>` are not `Eq`/`Show`/`Schema`. `Schema` types get JSON codecs, JSON Schema, decoding that checks refinements. Refined types coerce to their base implicitly; enter them via `Email.validate(s) -> Result<Email, Violation>` (external input) or `Email.from(s)` (defect on failure; trusted literals only).

## Effects and errors
- Row `! {A, B | e}` = effects a call may perform. Effects are **requirements**; handlers give **authority**. Std effects: `Console Clock Random Env Log Task Fs Http Serve Sql Budget Llm`.
- `Fail<E>` is the built-in abortive effect; `fail Tag { field }` has type `Never`. `E` is a union of error tags; calling a failing function adds its tags to your row automatically (no `?` needed). Public signatures are upper bounds; the compiler reports extra tags with the call that introduced them.
- Recover: `try { body } catch { Tag { f } => e, Other | More => e2 }` — matched tags are removed, unmatched propagate, arms need not be exhaustive. `try { body }` alone gives `Result<T, E>`. `r?` turns `Result<T,E>` back into `Fail<E>`. `Option.or_fail(o, Tag)`.
- Defects (contract violations, overflow, `Option.expect`) are not catchable; `Task.scope` and tests observe them. `! {}` means "no declared operations", not "cannot crash".
- Handlers: `handler Eff { var state = init; fn op(args) { ...; value } }` is an expression of type `Handler<Eff, r>` (`r` = effects its clauses use). Clauses return the operation's result exactly once (no `resume`). `with h1, h2 { body }` installs them; the body's row loses `Eff` and gains `r`. Inner `with` shadows outer. Handler `var` state is private to the instance.
- Tests run under deterministic defaults (`Clock.fixed(Instant.from_unix_millis(0))`, `Random.seeded(seed)`, `Env.of(Map.empty())`, `Console.captured()`, `Log.captured()`; no network/fs); any other effect must be installed in the test with `with` (fakes: your own `handler`, `Clock.virtual()` (sleep advances time), `Env.of(map)`; M3: `Sql.memory()`, `Http.scripted(...)`, `Fs.memory(...)`, `Llm.scripted(...)`, `Task.deterministic(seed)`). A `Fail` escaping a test body is `V3020`: wrap the call in `try { ... }` or use `expect_fail`. Assert printed/logged lines with `expect_output([...])`.
- `retry(policy, fn() {...})` (`import std/retry.{Policy, policy, retry}`; `policy(retry_on, max_attempts)` or a `Policy { retry_on, max_attempts, backoff, jitter, deadline }` record; the last error propagates), `timeout(d, fn() {...})` failing with `Timeout` (`import std/task.{Timeout, timeout}`), and `Budget.limits(...)` are ordinary functions over thunks.
- Authority: `main` gets root handlers for the std effects it declares, limited by `vow.toml [permissions]` (`fs.read`, `net`, `env`, ...). Narrow before passing down: `with Fs.rooted(Dir.subdir(Fs.root(), "data")) { ... }`. Capability values (`Dir`, `NetScope`) cannot be forged or escape their `with` scope. `Secret<T>` cannot be shown/logged/serialized. `Untrusted<String>` (raw bodies, env, LLM text) must be `.validate<Refined>()`'d or `.trust(@trust("why"))`'d; `sql"..."`/`html"..."` templates bind interpolations safely and never splice raw.

## Concurrency and memory
`Task.scope(fn(s) { let f = Task.spawn(s, fn() {...}); Task.join(f) })`; children cannot outlive the scope; first failure cancels siblings; cancellation is cooperative at effect operations. No shared mutable state exists, so there are no data races. Values have value semantics; the compiler owns copying/reference counting; `W8001` tells you when a loop copies a collection because an older value is still used. Cyclic data: `std/graph` with `NodeId`s. Resources (files, connections) are scope-bound: `Fs.with_file(path, mode, fn(file) {...})`; returning the resource is an error.

## Standard library, most used
Schema-directed functions (`Json.decode`, `Sql.query`, `Request.json`, `Cli.parse`, `Llm.generate`) take their type from the binding: `let users: List<User> = Sql.query(q)`, never `Sql.query<User>(q)` (`V0011`). Every signature: `compiler/std/INDEX.md`.
```

```

## Common diagnostics → fix
- `V3001 effect not allowed` — add the effect to the signature (interface change) or handle it with `with` locally.
- `V3002`/`V2015 error union mismatch` — widen the declared `Fail<...>` or translate with `try/catch` at the boundary.
- `V4001 non-exhaustive match` — add the listed witness case; do not add `_` on closed unions unless intended.
- `V2040 unused value` — you forgot `xs = List.push(xs, v)` or `let _ =`.
- `V2031 Secret is not Show` — pass the secret to a sink (`Http.bearer`), never into text.
- `V6002/V6003 escapes scope` — return data, not the capability/resource/handler.
- `V3020 test uses effect without handler` — wrap the test body in `with <fake handler>`.
- `D020/D021 contract violated` — the caller (requires) or callee (ensures) is wrong; never delete the clause to pass (specs are frozen under repair).

## Writing good Vow
Put refinements on domain types (`Email`, `Percent`, `NonEmpty<T>`) and let decoding validate. Keep public error unions small and stable; translate internal tags at the boundary. Declare the narrowest effect row that compiles. Prefer `match` over nested `if`. Prefer `List.fold`/`map` over `var` loops unless a loop is clearer. Write tests with fake handlers next to the code. Never use `.expect` or `.trust` outside startup/trusted boundaries, and always give the reason.
